$what: Every commit subject between the audit baseline and today that does NOT conform, so the next one is visible against a known floor instead of joining a count that nobody reads.
$why: These two are pushed to a shared branch that parallel sessions have checked out. Fixing a subject means rewriting the commit, which means a force push, which silently destroys whatever another session has on top of it. The subject is the one part of a commit with no runtime effect at all, so the trade is real damage against cosmetics. Freezing them and refusing the NEXT one is the only disposition that changes anything.
$rules: classifyCommitSubject in scripts/final-audit-lib.mjs. The gate: scripts/final-audit.mjs, seventh row.
$how_to_shrink_this: You cannot fix an entry, only outlive it. A SHA leaves this file when it falls behind FINAL_AUDIT_GIT_BASE, which happens the next time the audit baseline is moved forward at a release. The gate fails on a SHA that is no longer in range, so this file cannot quietly keep names of commits nobody measures.
